Product tasks are the UI wave's phases 0 and 1 (docs/art/ui-quality/report.md section 3.3: steps 1-4 in phase 0; steps 4-7, AD's board 1 and flow review in phase 1). Phase 1 started on 4 November 2026 by the owner's order 3 (CLAUDE.md), with D13's answer (c): at most three UI builders at once, icon batches 3 and 4 deferred (not filed). SV's are the owner's server decisions (docs/decisions/owner-decisions.md, 'Build tasks'); BT's are the protocol's build tasks. O2 and O3 were the owner's reviews; since 30 October 2026 AD does them as ordinary tasks (report.md section 3.4), so no task waits for the owner. The order of 'tasks' is priority. building_cap is three UI builders (D-05, D13 (c)) plus SV, approved by the owner on 30 October 2026. Phase 2 started on 12 November 2026 (lead cycle 70): P1-AD-board-1d let board 1 stand and phase 1's other exit criteria hold (report.md section 3.2); its first tasks are the flow findings (S1, S2) and board 1's note G (AIA-2), within the same cap of three. From the owner (phase 1 lessons, progress report KPIs, measured at main 40f91dfd). Four phase 1 KPIs missed their targets; carry these rules into phase 2's seeding and cycles. (1) Scope grew +22h (38% over the 58h planned; limit 10%): the pilot heist took 5 parts and board 1 took 4 rounds, because the art director's objections came after the work was finished, one round at a time. When you seed a screen or a board, estimate it with one review round included, and put in its done_when that AD previews the stills before ready (see M12). (2) All 5 of phase 1's first-attempt misses (24 of 29 merged at first attempt, target 90% or more) came from a list or a baked file that had gone out of step with another task's work: the catalogue's SKINS_OF list twice, kit art 2a's new skins without a SKINS_OF entry, kit art 2c against the kit's list of materials with no baked shape, and the high-contrast icon atlas not rebaking to its sources (twice). When two tasks share such a list or derived file, make one depend on the other, or put both changes in one task, and build every candidate from current main. (3) Pace was 1.02h of work an hour against 1.2 needed. Seed phase 2's remaining steps (report.md 3.3: motion art, screens, boards 2-5) now, so each builder has its next task open before its current one merges and none of the three slots sits empty. (4) Several of your checks failed on the container, not the work (no wasm32 target, no Godot, no node_modules, no native library in the candidate's folder). At the start of each cycle, run the fresh-container setup line from M3, then bash client/build.sh in the candidate worktree, before any check_all or guard.sh. Add M10 to acks when read.

From the owner (12 November 2026, about 20:00Z, in the overseer session's chat): "Yes, raise it to 4 builders." CLAUDE.md order 3 now sets the cap at four UI builders. It drops back to three on its own while the seven-day bar reads allowed_warning: start no fourth builder then, and let a running fourth one finish its task. Why: at 19:12Z phase 2 had 49.8 hours left before its 14 November 21:00Z stop and 50.5 hours of seeded work, so the pace (1.02 hours of work an hour) had no slack; a fourth builder adds about 0.34. (1) On your next cycle, start a fourth builder if only three run. S1, S2 and S3 run now. AIA waits on AIA-R23, which is not blocking and whose default is that the sheet stands. So the first choice is to restart AIA on P2-AIA-motion-1 under that default: it unblocks P2-K1-motion, P2-AIA-motion-2 and P2-S1-result-2. If AIA cannot take the place, give it to the next open task with no unmet deps whose claims are disjoint from the running tasks (owners.py claims), the longest chain first. (2) Batching, from now (agent-protocol.md, 'Batching'): as soon as two or more tasks are ready at once, merge 2-3 with disjoint claims into one candidate; if it fails, re-check each alone. Do not wait for the 2-hour mark: phase 1's median wait from ready to merged was 2.1 hours. Add M15 to acks when read.

Lesson from UI phase 2 (P2-S2-flow-home, cycle 71). The first check_all on candidate 1e438a19 failed one fixture in tools/test_run_checks.sh ("and makes no worktree and no log") although S2 touches no runner file; the re-run on the same sha passed. Your write-up names the likely cause: the planted and refused test repos have the same tree and the same identity, so two commits made in the same second share a sha. The rule: (1) tools/test_run_checks.sh is yours (no task in flight owns it). Make its two test repos differ, with a distinct author identity, commit time or file in each, so their shas cannot collide; do it yourself between merges or seed a small K1 task for it. Never loosen, skip or delete the fixture. (2) Until that fix is on main, a lone FAIL of that fixture on a candidate that touches no runner file is re-run once on the same sha; a second FAIL is real. (3) Two lessons are past their ack_by and unread because their agents are waiting: deliver M12 to AD and M14 to AIA-2 in the prompt when you next start or resume them, and have them ack it in their status files.

Lesson from UI phase 2 (P2-S1-toon-drop, cycle 74). The wait from ready to merged rated worse for the second push in a row: 3.0h for P2-K1-motion, then 2.7h for the toon drop (ready 23:41, merged 02:21). Three causes, all in the merge queue. At 23:41 three tasks were ready at once with disjoint claims (P2-S3-screenkit ready 22:59, P2-K1-motion ready 22:40, P2-S1-toon-drop ready 23:41), yet they were merged one at a time, against the batching rule you acked as M15. P2-K1-motion's merge reached main at 01:40, 51 minutes after its check passed at 00:49. And the toon drop's first check_all stopped on a read-only cargo lock because it was started inside the candidate's worktree, where client/ext/target is a link; the re-run from the main checkout passed. The rule: (1) As soon as two or more tasks are ready with disjoint claims, merge 2 or 3 of them into one candidate, as agent-protocol.md "Batching" says; if the batch fails, re-check each alone. (2) Merge to main and clear the lock in the same turn the check passes, then lock the next candidate in that turn. (3) Start check_all from the main checkout on the candidate sha, never from inside the candidate's worktree, or give that worktree its own writable CARGO_TARGET_DIR. (4) Add M17 to the acks in status/lead.json.

Lesson from the UI report (Work delivered rated worse two pushes in a row: 1.10, then 1.11 hours of work an hour against 1.2). Builder seats sit empty while a builder's session waits idle on its own request until its lease lapses: S2 from about 01:10 to its restart at 02:43 on 13 November, and AIA idle on AIA-R25 until its lease lapsed at 04:43. The rule: each cycle, check every builder's session with get_session.
